reason: The cited evidence (E1, E2) demonstrates that DeepMD potentials were trained on AIMD data for both crystalline and liquid states of a high-entropy carbonitride using active learning (DP-GEN), supporting the feasibility of the approach. However, the evidence does not directly compare the resulting potential's performance to EAM potentials, nor does it quantify improvements in phase-space overlap or thermodynamic integration path mismatch, leaving the key mechanistic and comparative premises unsupported by the cited passages.
premises: Deep learning potentials (e.g., DeepMD) can be trained on ab initio MD data for both solid and liquid configurations of high-entropy materials.
Active learning (e.g., DP-GEN) can iteratively incorporate rare and complex atomic configurations from ab initio liquid and solid phases into the training set.
A deep learning potential trained via active learning will better represent the many disordered atomic configurations of the ab initio liquid than conventional EAM potentials.
Better representation of liquid configurations by the reference potential increases phase-space overlap with the ab initio target in thermodynamic integration.
Increased phase-space overlap reduces the thermodynamic integration path mismatch relative to an EAM reference.
